description: Erection of a part single storey, part two storey extension to the side/rear, conversion of roof space to habitable use to include a rear dormer, 3 x roof lights, conversion of roof from hip to gable end.
decision_conditions: The proposal, by reason of overall scale, bulk, massing and proximity to the side boundary, would result in an incongruous and visually intrusive form of development that could not be considered to respect the architectural composition of the existing dwellinghouse and the pair of semi-detached properties. The proposed development would also fail to harmonise with the established built environment along Warwick Crescent resulting in a detrimental impact on the character and appearance of the street scene. The proposal would therefore be contrary to Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One - Strategic Policies (2012), Policies DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two- Development Management Policies (2020) Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), and Chapter 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposal, by reason of its excessive scale bulk and siting, would represent an oppressive and overbearing form of development which would detract from the residential amenities of the occupants of adjacent 114 Warwick Avenue, in conflict with policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and policies DMHB11 and DMHD1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two- Development Management Policies (2020).

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.
